What this means

Five takeaways

  1. Diriyah ecosystem runs on third-party paid social — DarGlobal at 120 ads dominates Wadi Safar messaging.
  2. Diriyah Company itself has zero active Meta ads in SA; recovery requires fixing disclaimer compliance first.
  3. Red Sea Global's 570-ad scale is the benchmark — every other developer is an order of magnitude behind.
  4. ROSHN's Meta absence is intentional; brand depends on owned channels and broker amplification (Expat Key).
  5. Drop the 6-platform conceit — TikTok / X / LinkedIn / Snap have no public signal and add nothing to the picture.
Methodology · sources · dropped platforms

Method

  • Each Meta count is a PAGE-SCOPED banner number, captured from the Meta Ad Library with view_all_page_id=<id>&country=SA. The banner shows e.g. '~120 results' which is the source of truth.
  • We confirmed each page_id by visiting an ad detail page (?id=<lid>) and reading the page_id JSON from the ad's owner. v2 mis-attributed many ads from keyword leaks; v3 uses verified page_id mappings.
  • Active vs inactive splits use Meta's status filter active_status=active or =inactive.
  • Last-6-month splits use start_date[min]=2025-11-06.
  • Dropped TikTok / X / LinkedIn / Snap because they are auth-walled, deprecated, or expose only political ads. Replaced with SimilarWeb traffic share + Google Trends interest as directional cross-channel signal.
  • Numbers are precise to the banner (Meta rounds to nearest 5/10/100 for high-volume pages). All figures captured 2026-05-06.

Dropped platforms

  • tiktok — Commercial ad library renders empty under unauth headless browsing; not publicly indexable in 2026.
  • x_twitter — Twitter Ad Library deprecated; ads.x.com transparency endpoints return empty bodies.
  • linkedin — LinkedIn Ad Library requires sign-in; no public crawl possible.
  • snap — snap.com/political-ads exposes political ads only; commercial inventory not indexed.
